## Purpose and Runtime Topology
Modly is a local, GPU-backed desktop application that converts images into 3D meshes using installable open-source model extensions. It combines an Electron desktop shell, React renderer, and Python/FastAPI compute backend; no cloud inference service is required. Primary desktop entry points are `electron/main/index.ts`, `src/main.tsx`, and `api/main.py`.

## Desktop Shell and Native Boundary
Electron owns application lifecycle, persistent settings, OS integration, embedded-Python setup, backend process launching, downloads, updates, and artifact registration. Renderer access is mediated through the preload/IPC boundary rather than direct Node access. Key paths: `electron/main/ipc-handlers.ts`, `electron/main/python-bridge.ts`, `electron/preload/electron-api.ts`.

## Renderer Application
The React/Vite UI routes among setup, generation, models/extensions, settings, and workflow editing. Shared stores coordinate application, agent, extension, navigation, and workflow state. The generation area presents image input, model/workflow controls, progress, asset library, and 3D/splat viewers. Key paths: `src/App.tsx`, `src/shared/router/Router.tsx`, `src/areas/generate/GeneratePage.tsx`.

## API and Generation Orchestration
FastAPI exposes the backend contract consumed by Electron/renderer and automation clients. Routers separate generation, model management, extensions, optimization/export, settings/status, agent endpoints, and workflow-run lifecycle. Generator implementations are selected through a registry; the backend runner executes generation work. Key paths: `api/main.py`, `api/routers/workflow_runs.py`, `api/services/generator_registry.py`, `api/runner.py`.

## Extension and Model Boundary
Models and processing capabilities are external extensions, generally acquired from GitHub and described by `manifest.json`. Electron performs installation/path validation and lifecycle work; Python launches or coordinates extension processes. This isolates arbitrary model runtime dependencies from the core application and allows model variants/downloads. Key paths: `electron/main/extension-install-utils.ts`, `electron/main/extension-path-guard.ts`, `api/services/extension_process.py`.

## Workflow Execution and Mesh Processing
Users compose validated node graphs, then run them from the Generate page. Nodes cover inputs, image/text, extension execution, loops/waits, mesh loading, preview, and scene insertion; built-in processing extensions provide export, optimization, remeshing, repair, and smoothing. Invalid wiring is preflighted before execution and should preserve the current scene. Key paths: `src/areas/workflows/WorkflowsPage.tsx`, `src/areas/workflows/preflight.ts`, `src/areas/workflows/workflowRunStore.ts`, `src/areas/workflows/nodes/mesh-optimizer/processor.ts`.

## Native Geometry Pipeline and Automation
The Python backend includes compiled native modules for UV unwrapping and texture baking, with C++ plus CUDA/Metal platform implementations—important GPU/platform boundaries. A stdlib-only CLI automates a running desktop app through canonical API concepts, especially workflow-run polling and final artifact export. Key paths: `api/uv_unwrapper/uv_unwrapper/unwrap.py`, `api/texture_baker/texture_baker/baker.py`, `tools/modly-cli/agent.py`.
